To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ATG5 is induced upon exposure of cancer cells to DNA damaging agents.
DNA damaging agents, such as etopo- side and cisplatin activate autophagy in cancer cells.
ATG5 is induced in response to DNA damage and promotes mitotic cell death independent of autophagic activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of autophagy and the molecular pathways leading to mitotic catastrophe.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the cellular responses to anticancer drug therapy.
the role of autophagy in the response to DNA damaging drugs and the molecular mechanisms underlying ATG5 induced mitotic catastrophe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATG5 is a key player in DNA damage induced mitotic catastrophe, and that this is independent of its autophagy promoting function.
ATG5 promotes both autophagic and apoptotic cell death in a cell type and drug dependent manner.
autophagy and mitotic catastrophe induced by DNA damaging drugs are independent processes and that ATG5 is an essential factor for both.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autophagy is not just a mechanism to remove damaged cells, it can also be a driver of cell death.
autophagy related proteins, such as ATG5, can be activated by DNA damaging agents, and this activation is independent of autophagic cell death.
autophagy related proteins can also be involved in the induction of mitotic cell death, which is a novel mechanism of cell death in response to DNA damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATG5 expression is induced by DNA damage and promotes mitotic cell death independently of autophagy.
ATG5 expression and localization are critical determinants of cell fate in response to DNA damage.
ATG5 plays a role in both autophagic and cell death signalling in response to DNA damage, which has important implications for the use of ATG5 inhibitors in the context of cancer therapy.
